answer: The system resists Sybil attacks by clustering identities whose measurements match, so clones from one operator are paid together as one. Each holder climbs a 20-meter knoll while a sensor records one pulse every 10 seconds, then waits 60 seconds on a terrace at the top while readings are compared with other identities; a pulse pattern within 2 percent of another, a climb under 5 minutes, or a missing reading merges them into one cluster for 30 days, so 100 fakes earn no more than one unless each makes a separate climb with a distinct pattern.
